subject: ela
intro: Authors reveal characters through what they think, what they say, and what they do. To describe a character in depth means naming a trait, like brave or stubborn, and backing it up with a specific thought, word, or action from the text. You can describe a setting the same way, using details of the time and place and how they affect the story. You can also describe an event by explaining what happens, why it happens, and what it leads to. In every case, do not just say what a character or place is like. Point to the exact detail that shows it.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the fire alarm blared, the little kids in the hallway froze. Fourth-grader Imani did not. She knelt down, made her voice calm and steady, and said, "Everybody take my hand, we are going to walk outside together like a train." She led the whole line to the field without a single tear.

Describe Imani using a specific detail from the story.

steps: Name a trait: Imani is calm and takes charge in an emergency.
Find the action or words that prove it.
She keeps her voice "calm and steady" and leads the kids out "like a train."
solution.answer: Imani is calm and a natural leader. When the little kids froze, she knelt down, kept her voice "calm and steady," and told them to take her hand and walk outside "like a train," leading them all to safety without panic.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The old bookshop sat at the end of a narrow alley where the sun never quite reached. Dust floated in the thin light, and the shelves leaned so close together that two people could not pass. It smelled of paper and rain. Somewhere in the back, a clock that had not worked in years still ticked, though no one could say how.

Describe the setting of this story in depth, using specific details.

steps: Name the place: a shadowy, old bookshop in a narrow alley.
Gather sensory details of time and place.
The dim light, dust, leaning shelves, and the mysterious ticking clock create a mysterious, old feeling.
solution.answer: The setting is a dim, old bookshop at the end of a narrow alley "where the sun never quite reached." Details like the floating dust, shelves "so close together that two people could not pass," the smell of "paper and rain," and a broken clock that "still ticked" make it feel mysterious and forgotten by time.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Diego had promised to water the neighbor's garden while she was away, but on the hottest day he wanted to go to the pool with his friends. He stood at the gate, towel over his shoulder, then turned around, filled the watering can, and soaked every row before he left. His friends had to wait, but the tomatoes did not die.

Describe the event at the gate and what it shows about Diego.

steps: Describe what happens: Diego almost skips his chore for the pool but turns back to water the garden.
Explain why it matters: he keeps his promise even when tempted.
Name the trait his action reveals.
solution.answer: At the gate, Diego is tempted to leave for the pool but turns around and waters "every row" before going. The event shows he is responsible and keeps his promises, since he puts the neighbor's garden ahead of his own fun even on "the hottest day."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

"I do not need help," Grandpa muttered, waving away the cane the doctor offered. He gripped the railing instead, climbing the porch steps one slow, stubborn inch at a time, sweat on his forehead. "I have climbed these steps for fifty years," he said, "and I will climb them fifty more."

Describe Grandpa, using both his words and his actions as evidence.

steps: Name a trait: Grandpa is stubborn and proud.
Find his words: "I do not need help" and "I will climb them fifty more."
Find his actions: he waves away the cane and climbs slowly on his own.
solution.answer: Grandpa is stubborn and proudly independent. His words "I do not need help" and "I have climbed these steps for fifty years, and I will climb them fifty more" show his pride, and his action of waving away the cane to climb "one slow, stubborn inch at a time" proves he refuses to accept help.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every time the class had a hard question, Priya was the first to raise her hand, even when she was not sure of the answer. Once she gave a wrong reply and a few kids snickered. Priya just shrugged and said, "Now I know one way that does not work," and her hand shot up again on the very next question.

Describe Priya using a specific detail from the text.

steps: Name a trait: Priya is confident and unafraid to be wrong.
Find the proof: after a wrong answer she says, "Now I know one way that does not work."
Her hand shoots up again, showing she is not discouraged.
solution.answer: Priya is confident and not afraid of being wrong. After giving a wrong answer and being snickered at, she shrugs and says, "Now I know one way that does not work," then raises her hand again on the next question, showing she treats mistakes as part of learning.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The campground at dawn was still and gray, the lake as smooth as glass. Frost clung to the tent ropes, and every breath hung in a little cloud. Then the sun crested the ridge, and all at once the mist lifted, birds began to call, and the whole valley turned gold.

Describe how the setting changes from the beginning to the end, using details.

steps: Describe the first setting: still, gray, frosty, cold at dawn.
Describe the change when the sun rises.
The mist lifts, birds call, and the valley turns gold.
solution.answer: The setting changes from cold and quiet to warm and lively. At first the campground is "still and gray" with frost on the tent ropes and breath hanging "in a little cloud." When the sun crests the ridge, "the mist lifted, birds began to call, and the whole valley turned gold," making it feel alive and bright.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The two rivals, Cole and Nasir, both wanted the last spot on the science team. During the final challenge, Nasir's model collapsed. Cole could have stayed quiet and won. Instead he crossed the room, knelt beside Nasir, and helped him rebuild it. They both finished, and the teacher chose them both.

Describe the key event and explain what it reveals about Cole.

steps: Describe the event: during the challenge, Cole helps his rival Nasir rebuild a collapsed model.
Note the choice: Cole could have won by staying quiet.
Name what it reveals about him.
solution.answer: The key event is Cole helping his rival Nasir rebuild his collapsed model instead of staying quiet to win. This reveals that Cole is fair and kind, valuing helping a competitor over winning alone, and his choice leads the teacher to pick them both.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Whenever something went wrong, Marcus blamed everyone but himself. He lost the game ball and said the grass was too tall. He failed the quiz and said the teacher wrote it unfairly. But when his little sister broke his model plane and started to cry, Marcus surprised even himself. "It is okay," he said. "It was already cracked. I should have put it up higher."

Describe how Marcus behaves at first and how his behavior changes, using details.

steps: At first Marcus blames others: the tall grass, the unfair teacher.
Then his sister breaks his plane and he does not blame her.
He takes responsibility, showing a change.
solution.answer: At first Marcus refuses to take blame, saying "the grass was too tall" and "the teacher wrote it unfairly." But when his sister breaks his plane, he changes, telling her "It is okay... I should have put it up higher," which shows him taking responsibility instead of blaming someone else.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The throne room was nothing like Tessa had imagined. Instead of gold and marble, the walls were plain stone hung with children's drawings. The queen sat not on a high throne but on a low wooden stool, mending a torn cloak by candlelight. "A crown," the queen said without looking up, "is heavier than it looks."

Describe both the setting and the queen, and explain how the details connect.

steps: Describe the setting: a plain stone throne room with children's drawings and candlelight.
Describe the queen: humble, sitting on a stool, mending a cloak herself.
Connect them: the simple room matches her humble, hardworking character.
solution.answer: The setting is a surprisingly plain throne room with "walls... hung with children's drawings" and candlelight instead of gold and marble. The queen matches it: she sits on "a low wooden stool, mending a torn cloak" herself. The humble room and her humble actions connect to show she is a modest, hardworking ruler, hinted at by her words that a crown "is heavier than it looks."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

At the start of camp, Wren refused to get in the canoe, sure she would tip it over. She sat on the dock for three days watching. On the fourth day, she quietly climbed in, paddled a shaky circle, then a smoother one. By the last day of camp, she was the one steadying the canoe for the newest, most frightened camper.

Describe how Wren changes across the story, using specific details from beginning, middle, and end.

steps: Beginning: Wren is fearful and refuses the canoe, watching from the dock.
Middle: she quietly climbs in and paddles shaky circles.
End: she steadies the canoe for a frightened newcomer, showing she has grown brave and helpful.
solution.answer: Wren changes from fearful to confident. At the beginning she "refused to get in the canoe" and watched from the dock for three days. In the middle she climbs in and paddles "a shaky circle, then a smoother one." By the end she is "steadying the canoe for the newest, most frightened camper," showing she has overcome her fear and now helps others.
